body:
## Purpose

Fuse the GPU-heavy parts of the AMIP prognostic EDMF + 1M step into per-column loops (`DataLayouts.foreach_column`), so pointwise derivatives, face densities, and band products become loop temporaries instead of separate broadcasts and scratch fields. This needs ClimaCore 1.0.8.

## Content

- `perf/benchmark_components.jl`: a component-level GPU timing and equivalence harness for the `numerics_sphere_he16ze63.yml` + `amip_target.yml` configuration, plus helpers shared by the fused loops.
- Fused column loops for:
  - the implicit vertical transport: water sedimentation, the SGS mass flux, SGS vertical advection and sedimentation, and the grid-mean vertical advection;
  - the precomputed quantities and caches: 1M precipitation velocities, the EDMFX environment, draft, and explicit closures, the SGS covariance cache, cloud and precipitation fractions, and the eddy-diffusion closures. 1M microphysics skips dry cells;
  - the explicit tendencies: hyperdiffusion, surface flux, sponge, TKE, explicit vertical advection, RRTMGP radiation, and the SGS diffusive flux;
  - the manual sparse Jacobian: advection, sedimentation, diffusion, SGS advection, entrainment/detrainment, and the SGS mass flux.
- The updraft sedimentation of #4926 (mass, enthalpy, and dilution terms, and their Jacobian blocks) runs in these loops with the operation order of main's broadcasts. The SGS advection Jacobian uses one column loop per sedimenting species, since a single loop would pass more arguments than Julia unrolls in a splat (a dynamic call on GPU).
- Fixes:
  - `horizontal_tracer_advection_tendency!` advected draft 1's tracers once per draft and the other drafts' tracers not at all. It now advects each draft's own tracers.
  - Four fused bodies now group floating-point operations in the same order as the unfused code.
  - Functions the fusions left unused are removed.
- Bumps ClimaCore to 1.0.8 and the reference counter.

## Component benchmark

`perf/benchmark_components.jl Float32` on one A100, timing GPU µs over 15 samples after 3 warmups. Compared: main `78abddd6d` vs. this PR at `dc65d98a7`. Both sides use this branch's manifest (ClimaCore 1.0.6, CloudMicrophysics 0.47), so the speedups come from the ClimaAtmos changes alone. The two runs were made one after the other on a node shared with other users; absolute times on that node varied by up to 1.7x between runs, so treat individual ratios as approximate.

### Equivalence with main

Maximum relative difference for 25 state, tendency, Jacobian-solve, and precomputed quantities, from `compute_refs` in the harness:

- **Bit-identical (23):** `Y.c` and `Y.f` after `initialize_implicit_stage_problem!`, implicit `Yₜ.f`, `invert_jacobian!` `ΔY.f`, remaining `Yₜ.c` and `Yₜ.f`, `Yₜ_lim.c`, `Yₜ.c` (correct_implicit), `ᶠK_h`, `ᶠK_u`, `ᶜgradᵥ_θ_liq_ice`, `ᶜgradᵥ_q_tot`, `ᶜcloud_fraction`, `ᶜprecip_frac`, `ᶜsgs_moments`, `ᶜl_mix`, `ᶜT′T′`, `ᶜq′q′`, `ᶜcorr_Tq`, `ᶜα`, `ᶜmp_tendency⁰`, and the surface rain and snow fluxes.
- **Roundoff level, within the harness's 1e-5 Float32 tolerance:**

| Quantity | max relative difference |
|---|---|
| implicit `Yₜ.c` | 8.44e-07 |
| `invert_jacobian!` `ΔY.c` | 1.46e-06 |

On CPU, the fused updraft sedimentation tendency and Jacobian are bit-identical to main's broadcasts on a perturbed AMIP h_elem 4 state, and 20 steps of four EDMF and single-column configurations (TRMM 1M and 0M, BOMEX with a passive tracer, single-column precipitation) are bit-identical to main. DYCOMS RF02 differs at roundoff from step ~10, as it did before this rebase.

To reproduce, run `perf/benchmark_components.jl` in `save` mode on main, then in `compare` mode on this branch.

body: Restores two behaviors that #4934 changed: `sfc_tke` in the fused covariance loop holds the local TKE (see https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaAtmos.jl/pull/4934#discussion_r4439224249), and `ᶜbuoygrad` is never written for an EDMF model without covariances, which leaves `ᶜl_mix` uninitialized.
title: fix: restore the surface TKE and the buoyancy gradient after #4934

## Purpose 
<!--- One sentence to describe the purpose of this PR, refer to any linked issues:
#14 -- this will link to issue 14
Closes #2 -- this will automatically close issue 2 on PR merge
-->
With `ImplicitCloudLiquidFormation` and prognostic EDMF, the implicit-stage predictor (`solve_sgs_updraft_tracers_implicit_stage_analytic!`) condensed `Δq_lcl = τ(1 − exp(−dtγ/τ)) S` into the updraft `q_lcl` but left the grid-mean `ρq_lcl` unchanged. With one Newton iteration and no `(ρq_lcl, q_lclʲ)` Jacobian block, the grid mean only received `ρaʲ S` evaluated at the already-saturated predictor state, so the environment `q_lcl` of the stage fell by `ρaʲ Δq_lcl / ρa⁰`, and `enforce_edmf_updraft_constraints!` (`edmfx_filter`) clipped the updraft `q_lcl` to `ρq_lcl / ρa`. The `u₃` solve still saw the condensed, buoyant predictor state.

In `prognostic_edmfx_bomex_column` (ARS222, dt 120 s, 1 Newton iteration) with `ImplicitCloudLiquidFormation` and `condensation_evaporation_timescale = 10`, the updraft `q_lcl` was exactly 0 in 76 % of updraft samples above 600 m, with the updraft 15–40 % supersaturated and 1–4 K colder than the environment. The clip fired at 94–97 % of stages and removed ~95 % of the updraft liquid. dt 60 s, explicit condensation, a 100 s timescale, or 3 Newton iterations did not show it.

The predictor now adds `ρaʲ Δq_lcl` to the grid-mean `ρq_lcl`, in the last Picard round only (the loop restores the updraft scalars between rounds but not the grid mean).

body:
## Summary

Stretched vertical grids (`z_stretch: true`) use ClimaCore's two-scale `Meshes.BoundaryLayerHyperbolicTangentStretching` (CliMA/ClimaCore.jl#2709), which refines the boundary layer with scale height `z_pbl` (new key, default 2200 m) while matching the layer thickness `dz_bottom` at the surface and `dz_top` (new key, default 3000 m) at the model top. The keys flow from `default_config.yml` through `get_grid` to `SphereGrid`, `ColumnGrid`, `BoxGrid`, and `PlaneGrid`, whose vertical mesh the new `get_z_mesh` builds.

The rule admits `z_elem` within a range set by `dz_bottom`, `dz_top`, `z_pbl`, and `z_max`. Outside that range, ClimaCore's mesh constructor raises an `ArgumentError` that names the range, and `get_z_mesh` lets it propagate. The 10-level default grid lies below the range (its mean spacing equals `dz_top`), so the grid constructors default to `z_stretch = false`.

Adds the 79-level configurations `numerics_sphere_he24ze79.yml` and `numerics_column_ze79.yml`, and tests of the uniform, fine, custom-`dz_top`, and rejected cases.

## Configuration changes

Every Buildkite job was classified against the real constructor (YAML-parsed pipelines, including `commands:` steps and `JOB_NAME` expansion): 27 jobs run two-scale, 59 uniform, none rejected.

- 31 configs whose grids the rule rejects set `z_stretch: false` and drop their unused `dz_bottom`: the 10-level default grid (including `numerics_sphere_he6ze10.yml`), the 25-level `bm_*` perf grids, and the 50-level gray radiative-equilibrium column. The YAML default stays `z_stretch: true`.
- Three configs keep stretching with a `dz_top` inside the range the rule admits for them: `numerics_sphere_he6ze31.yml` (8000 m; range 6090 to 30000 m), the 200-level ERA5-driven column (500 m; range 490 to 500 m), and the RCEMIP box CRM (2000 m; range 840 to 2960 m).
- The shallow cases set a `dz_top` close to the top spacing they have on `main`, so the global 3000 m default does not coarsen them aloft: `larcform1_1M_prognostic_edmfx.yml` 250 m (9 km domain), the three `plane_*` tests 600 m (21 km, mountain waves), and `prognostic_edmfx_armvaranal_column.yml` 1000 m (15 km). Their maximum adjacent-layer ratios stay at or below 1.13.
- `single_column_hydrostatic_balance_ft64.yml` states `z_stretch: true` because CI pairs it with `numerics_sphere_he6ze10.yml`, which sets false.
- `reproducibility_tests/ref_counter.jl` is bumped: every stretched CI grid changes.

Known leftover: `bm_aquaplanet_progedmf.yml` runs alone on the rejected 25-level grid and also paired with `he6ze31`, so the paired benchmark runs uniform.

## Review notes

Spacing of the single-scale rule on `main` versus the two-scale rule with the chosen `dz_top`, computed against ClimaCore `main`:

| grid | `dz_top` [m] | top spacing [m] | levels below 2 km | max adjacent-layer ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ze63, 60 km, `dz_bottom` 30 m | 3000 (default) | 2864 → 3000 | 21 → 22 | 1.10 → 1.11 |
| he24ze79, 60 km, 28 m | 3000 (default) | 2210 → 3000 | 25 → 33 | 1.08 → 1.14 |
| `larcform1` column, 90 levels, 9 km, 10 m | 250 | 231 → 250 | 50 → 51 | 1.05 → 1.05 |
| `plane_*` tests, 100 levels, 21 km, 10 m | 600 | 578 → 600 | 46 → 47 | 1.06 → 1.06 |
| `armvaranal` column, 45 levels, 15 km, 30 m | 1000 | 797 → 1000 | 20 → 23 | 1.11 → 1.13 |
| ERA5 column, 200 levels, 45 km, 30 m | 500 | 481 → 500 | 42 → 47 | 1.02 → 1.02 |

The ERA5 column's admissible window (490 to 500 m) is set by packing 200 levels from 30 m over 45 km with `z_pbl = 2200` m; `z_pbl = 3000` m widens it only to 580 m. The chosen 500 m reproduces the spacing on `main` to within 4 percent at every level.

title: Use two-scale boundary-layer vertical stretching and add 79-level configs
